traveler: Otto Hanish (Ernst or Erich Otto Haenisch, styled Otoman Zar-Adusht Ha'nish)
title: Posen to Los Angeles: the Grocer's Son Who Became a Persian Magi, and the Breathing School That Reached the Bauhaus
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Veldes, the regime already running
stops.date_confidence: attested; inherited from arnold_rikli.journey.json, where this pin already stands
stops.campa: At the lake of Veldes in Carniola a Swiss dyer named Arnold Rikli declares sun and air a treatment and opens a cure house where patients walk uncovered in the light, drink water, and eat no meat. Water, air, light, a vegetable diet: the whole apparatus that the next century will call Lebensreform is assembled and working, a year before a grocer's son is born in Posen who will dress the same four elements in Zoroastrian costume and sell them to America. No text links the two men. The template does not need a courier.
suggested_refs: Rikli's Naturheilanstalt at Veldes, opened 1855, the atlas pin held by arnold_rikli.journey.json

stops.name: Poznan, birth in the provisions merchant's house
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In Posen, capital of the Prussian province of the same name, a son is born to Heinrich Ernst Haenisch, a provisions merchant, and his wife Anna Dorothea Schmidt. The registers as relayed do not agree on the boy's given names: the German article reads Erich Otto Haenisch, the English reads Ernst Otto Haenisch, and the disagreement is carried, not settled. He will spend his adult life insisting he was born twelve years earlier and four thousand kilometres to the south-east. This paper is the one document that makes the insistence a lie.
suggested_refs: The Prussian civil and parish registers of Posen for December 1856

stops.name: Poznan, the evangelical baptism
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and the confession; the church is unidentified and the pin is a conjecture
stops.campa: Nine days after the birth the child is baptized evangelical in Posen. The record names the confession and not the building; no source consulted names a church. The pin marks the square at Plac Wiosny Ludow where the Evangelical-Reformed church of St Peter stood from 1841 until the Battle of Poznan destroyed it in 1945, and that identification is offered as conjecture and nothing firmer. It is the last act of his life that a German parish clerk will witness and write down.
suggested_refs: The vanished Evangelical-Reformed St Peter's church at the Krysiewicza and Polwiejska corner, Poznan

stops.name: Tehran, the birth the movement will print
stops.date_confidence: legendary; the claimed day is 19 December 1844
stops.campa: The biography his followers will print begins here instead. Born on the nineteenth of December 1844 in Tehran, son of a Russian diplomat and a German noblewoman, an infant with a defective heart. David Ammann sets it down and the movement repeats it for eighty years. Nothing in any Persian, Russian, or Prussian record supports a syllable of it, and the Posen baptism of December 1856 contradicts it outright. The legend keeps the calendar day and moves the year and the continent. Both accounts stand here; neither dissolves the other.
suggested_refs: David Ammann's follower biography of Ha'nish, source of the Persian birth claim

stops.name: The Alborz highlands, the secret Zoroastrians
stops.date_confidence: legendary; the claimed period runs from infancy to about 1869 and no source fixes a year
stops.campa: The legend takes the sick child up into the Iranian mountains and gives him to a secret society of Zoroastrians, who teach him breath, diet, and the discipline that will keep his heart beating. He comes down a Magi. The English article reports only that he was sent as a child; the figure of twenty-five years circulating in later summaries is in neither Wikipedia and is dropped. No such community is attested anywhere. No evidence places Otto Haenisch on Persian ground at any point in his life.
suggested_refs: The Zoroastrian mountain-community motif in Mazdaznan's own literature

segments.name: The Crossing and the Trades Before the Prophet

stops.name: Port of New York, the crossing with no manifest
stops.date_confidence: undocumented; the 1880 pin is a placeholder inside a window that closes at 1890
stops.campa: Somewhere in these years the grocer's son crosses the Atlantic. No ship manifest, no port of entry, no year has been located. The English article says only that he settled in the United States; the German says he was living there by 1890 at the latest. The pin marks the harbour below the Battery where German emigrants of his decade came ashore at Castle Garden, and it marks nothing more than that. This is a hole in the record and it is entered here as a hole in the record.
suggested_refs: Castle Garden emigrant depot, New York, in operation until 1890

stops.name: Mendota, the sheep and the type case
stops.date_confidence: undated in the source; Sinclair gives no year at all and the pin is a placeholder before 1890
stops.campa: Upton Sinclair, writing in The Profits of Religion in 1918, puts him in Mendota, Illinois, and in a string of trades: sheep herder, typesetter, mesmerist, spiritualist. No year appears anywhere in the account, and the movement never corroborates a line of it. Sinclair is a hostile witness with a book to sell about religious fraud, and the English article hedges him accordingly. His version and the Persian version cannot both be true. The pages that would settle it were not opened in this pass.
suggested_refs: Upton Sinclair, The Profits of Religion (1918), pp. 278-281
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Otoman Zar-Adusht Ha'nish', summarizing Sinclair

stops.name: Chicago, the ten years that stand open
stops.date_confidence: contested; German Wikipedia says by 1890 at the latest, English Wikipedia says from 1900
stops.campa: The German article says he is living in the United States by 1890 at the latest, Chicago first. The English article says he lived in Chicago from 1900. Ten years stand open between the two sentences and nothing consulted closes them. Later summaries name a Mazdaznan Peace Centre founded here in 1890; that institution appears in no reachable source and is dropped from this journey. What is certain is only the city: a place where a man could arrive with an accent and a costume and be taken at his word.
suggested_refs: Chicago's West Side occult and health-reform circuit of the 1890s

stops.name: Chicago, the Art Institute and the words of welcome
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from swami_vivekananda.journey.json
stops.campa: In the Hall of Columbus of the Art Institute, Narendranath Datta rises as Swami Vivekananda before the World's Parliament of Religions and opens with sisters and brothers of America. The hall stands and applauds. Chicago learns in that fortnight that it has an appetite for imported prophets and for the East as a source of health, and the newspapers teach the rest of the country the same lesson. No source puts Haenisch in the room. He is in the same city, selling a Persian version of the same appetite inside the decade.
suggested_refs: The World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago, September 1893
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Parliament of the World's Religions'

stops.name: Zion, the church of John Alexander Dowie
stops.date_confidence: undated in the source; Dowie's Zion City is not founded until 1901, so the pin marks the church and not a visit
stops.campa: He is reported to have joined the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, then the Christian Catholic Apostolic Church, then James Brighouse's Mormon splinter. The second of those is John Alexander Dowie's, run out of Zion City on the Illinois lakeshore as a whole town under one faith healer, with tobacco, pork, and physicians forbidden inside the fence. The membership is in the source; nothing places Haenisch physically at Zion. He is learning the trade of the founder from founders.
suggested_refs: Zion City, Illinois, John Alexander Dowie's theocratic settlement

segments.name: Chicago: the Name, the Temple, the Journal

stops.name: 3016 Lake Park Avenue, the temple in the boat club
stops.date_confidence: address attested, start year undetermined; the temple is first documented in the 1912 proceedings
stops.campa: For many years he keeps a temple at 3016 Lake Park Avenue, in the old Farragut Boat Club house on the South Side. The English article gives the address with no starting year and dates his Chicago residence to 1900; the building enters the record as a temple only in the courtroom of 1912. Around this time he begins claiming a medical degree and lecturing on vegetarian diet and the cleansing of the intestine. No institution, faculty, or diploma has ever been identified behind the M.D.
stops.quote: The body is indeed the greatest of mechanisms and its adjustment assures the perfection of life.
stops.quote_source: Inner Studies: A Course of Twelve Lessons, Lesson One (1904 edition, archive.org 'inner_studies')
suggested_refs: The former Farragut Boat Club house, 3016 Lake Park Avenue, Chicago, built 1886
sources: Nominatim geocoding of 3016 S Lake Park Ave

stops.name: Chicago, the first number of the Sun-Worshiper
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1902 and to the Chicago area; no street address is given by any source
stops.campa: In February he brings out the first number of a monthly called Sun-Worshiper and signs it Otoman Zar-Adusht Ha'nish, the name he formally adopts this year. The apostrophe is doing heavy work. Zar-Adusht is Zarathustra, Mazdaznan is Ahura Mazda with a Zoroastrian suffix, and the whole vocabulary of Zoroaster's Good Religion is lifted intact from the Avesta and fitted over breathing exercises, bowel hygiene, and meatless cooking.
suggested_refs: Sun-Worshiper, monthly, Chicago, from February 1902

stops.name: New York City, the base the German record gives
stops.date_confidence: contested; German Wikipedia moves him here in 1902 while English Wikipedia has him in Chicago continuously from 1900
stops.campa: The German record moves his base of operations to New York this year. The English record has him running the Chicago temple without interruption from 1900 through the scandals of 1912. Both cannot be flatly true, no source consulted reconciles them, and no New York address survives in either. The contradiction is left standing where it was found. A man assembling a Persian identity out of an Illinois biography has reasons not to keep one fixed address in anybody's registry.
suggested_refs: The unlocated New York base of 1902 named only in the German article

stops.name: Chicago, the twelve lessons of Inner Studies
stops.date_confidence: contested; the bibliography dates the book 1902, the archive.org text reads 1904
stops.campa: Inner Studies: A Course of Twelve Lessons is the book that will do the most work for him and the most damage to him. Twelve lessons on breath, bathing, diet, and the passions, written in the voice of a physician who is not one. Lesson Two holds that a constipated person becomes of all people the most passionate, and Lesson Three that woman is the greatest factor in all life manifestations. In ten years a Chicago court and a Saxon police order will both name this volume by its title.
stops.quote: You cannot expect clean ideas from a person whose body is not clean.
stops.quote_source: Inner Studies: A Course of Twelve Lessons, Lesson Two (1904 edition, archive.org 'inner_studies')
suggested_refs: Inner Studies: A Course of Twelve Lessons, archive.org identifier inner_studies

stops.name: Chicago, the magazine describes its founder
stops.date_confidence: attested to the January 1906 issue
stops.campa: The movement's own magazine prints in its January number a follower's portrait of the founder at work. It appears under his editorship, which makes the sentence as much self-description as testimony. The Chicago operation now has a journal, a temple, a name, a costume, and a doctrine of breath. What it does not have, and will never acquire, is one independent witness to any part of the biography its founder tells about himself. Every source for the Persian childhood is a Mazdaznan source, and every Mazdaznan source is downstream of him.
stops.quote: He is continuously working, never stops a moment, but is never excited and is always calm, centered and self-contented.
suggested_refs: Mazdaznan magazine, January 1906, archive.org identifier mazdaznan_190601-gray

segments.name: The Mountain That Was Already There

stops.name: Monte Verita, the light-air huts
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from ida_hoffmann.journey.json
stops.campa: Above Ascona on Lago Maggiore, Ida Hofmann and Henri Oedenkoven raise light-air huts on a hill they name Monte Verita and run it on the same four elements as the Chicago temple: sun on bare skin, air, a vegetable diet, no alcohol. Neither party has heard of the other. Across the water Antoinette de Saint Leger keeps her two islands and her imported garden at Brissago. One doctrine surfaces in three places inside one decade with no courier passing between them.
suggested_refs: The light-air huts of Monte Verita, Ascona, from 1900

stops.name: Ascona, Vegetabilismus and Vegetarismus
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from the Ascona stop 'Vegetabilismus! Vegetarismus!' as it stands in ida_hoffmann.journey.json, not in engelmann.journey.json where the research lens reported it
stops.campa: Karl Max Engelmann keeps a vegetarian boarding house below the hill for two decades and founds a Pythagorean League, deriving from Porphyry a doctrine of purification by diet that arrives at exactly the table Hanish's Avestan one arrives at. Vegetabilismus, Vegetarismus: the words are printed on his own matter. Neither man's papers mention the other, and no meeting is attested anywhere. The kinship is one of type and of decade, and it is recorded here as nothing more than that.
suggested_refs: Engelmann's Pythagorean League and vegetarian pension above Locarno

stops.name: Monte Verita, Hermann Hesse climbs up
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from ida_hoffmann.journey.json
stops.campa: Hermann Hesse climbs the hill to dry out and comes down a chronicler of the place, writing up the vegetarians, the nudists, and the sun worshippers for German readers who would not otherwise believe such people exist. The publicity is what carries the life-reform vocabulary out of the Ticino and into the German-speaking cities. In the same season, two Swiss converts of a Chicago prophet are preparing to plant his version of it in Saxony. Hesse never records meeting a Mazdaznan and never names Hanish; the two stand on the same ground at different hours.
suggested_refs: Hesse's 1907 stay and his writings on the Monte Verita colony

segments.name: Leipzig: the Bridgehead Two Converts Built

stops.name: Leipzig, the Ammanns begin the lodges
stops.date_confidence: attested as the start of an open period; the German source reads von 1907 an, not a single year
stops.campa: David and Frieda Ammann carry the teaching from America into Germany and begin founding lodges: Leipzig, Dresden, Chemnitz, Weimar, Hamburg. The German source gives 1907 as the opening of a period, not a year in which five houses appeared at once. Hanish does not come. His movement crosses the ocean in the luggage of two converts while he stays in Illinois and California, and every penalty Europe imposes on Mazdaznan will be served by them. David Ammann was born at Honnavar in India in 1855; the summaries that call the pair former California farmers have him on the wrong continent.
suggested_refs: The first German Mazdaznan lodges at Leipzig, Dresden, Chemnitz, Weimar and Hamburg

stops.name: Leipzig, the doctrine arrives as a kitchen
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Ammann's German translation of the dietetic teaching appears as Diaetetik und Kochbuch, the first German edition, and the two men co-publish a magazine called Mazdaznan out of Leipzig. What arrives in German is not the Persian mysticism but the kitchen: whole grain against white flour, chewing, fasting, the bowel treated as the seat of character. Bread as most housewives now make it, the book says, could fittingly be dubbed the staff of death. German readers who will never accept a Persian prophet will accept a recipe, and the recipe is the vehicle.
stops.quote: The excessive use of white yeast bread is one of the prime causes of inebriety.
stops.quote_source: Mazdaznan Encyclopedia of Dietetics and Home Cook Book (archive.org 'mazdaznanencyclo00hani')
suggested_refs: Diaetetik und Kochbuch, Leipzig 1908, the first German Mazdaznan edition

stops.name: Schulstrasse 1, the lodge house changes orders
stops.date_confidence: date and street address attested exactly; the coordinates are approximate, no geocoder resolves the historic address
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of September the European central office opens at Schulstrasse 1, in the building the Masonic lodge Minerva zu den drei Palmen has vacated. A lodge house passes from one order to another without changing what it is for. From here the German editions go out and the lodges in five cities are supplied. The street is attested; the point on the globe is not, and sits at central Leipzig as an approximation stated as one. No geocoder consulted resolves the historic address, which now returns only a suburb five kilometres east.
suggested_refs: The former lodge house of Minerva zu den drei Palmen, Schulstrasse 1, Leipzig

stops.name: Leipzig, the single visit of 1911
stops.date_confidence: the crossing is attested, the destination is not; the German source names Europe and no city, and this pin is an inference
stops.campa: He crosses to Europe once, in 1911. The German source that records the crossing names no city, no host, and no date inside the year. The pin sits on Leipzig because Leipzig is where his organization then was, and the placement is an inference rather than a record. Four years of building by his converts he inspects, if he inspects it at all, in one visit. He will not come again for twelve years, and by then the man who received him will be dead and the German branch will have been thrown out of Saxony. A prophet with a European church who sets foot in Europe once in twenty-five years is running the operation by post.
suggested_refs: The 1911 European visit recorded without an itinerary in the German article

stops.name: Los Angeles, the free Sunday mornings
stops.date_confidence: contested; English Wikipedia dates his move here to 1908, German Wikipedia dates his settling to 1917
stops.campa: He begins giving free lectures on Sunday mornings in Los Angeles. The English record calls this a change of residence; the German record has him settling here only in 1917, and the Chicago temple runs through both accounts. Whether these are the years of a lecture circuit or of a second household is settled by nothing consulted. Southern California in 1908 is already the country's market for health doctrines, sanatoria, and sun cures, and he has found it early. The lectures are free, which is how the books are sold.
suggested_refs: Hanish's Sunday morning lecture series in Los Angeles from 1908

stops.name: 3016 Lake Park Avenue, the Billy Lindsay case
stops.date_confidence: attested to January 1912; the courtroom detail comes from contemporary press relayed by secondary sourcing not independently verified
stops.campa: Elizabeth Lindsay, a wealthy follower, has let her twelve-year-old son Billy travel with the teacher. The boy's uncle sues for custody, and in open court the passages of Inner Studies that describe tantric sexual practice are read into the record. The Chicago papers print them. In a fortnight a breathing and diet school on Lake Park Avenue becomes a matter for the federal postal inspectors, and the sentence about clean bodies and clean ideas is quoted back at the man who wrote it.
suggested_refs: The 1912 Lindsay custody proceedings and the reading of Inner Studies into the record
sources: contemporary Chicago press as summarized in secondary sourcing on the Farragut Boat Club building

stops.name: Chicago, the postal statute
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The temple is raided. He is convicted of sending obscene literature through the mail, fined two thousand five hundred dollars, and sentenced to six months. The charge is not the doctrine and not the boy: it is the postal statute, the instrument American courts of the period reach for when a religion prints what a jury will not read aloud. He serves it and continues. In Leipzig the central office, eighteen months old, publishes nothing about any of it.
suggested_refs: United States postal obscenity prosecutions of religious publishers, 1900-1920

stops.name: Chicago, the Dietetics and Cookery Book
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1914
stops.campa: Two years after the mail conviction he publishes the Mazdaznan Dietetics and Cookery Book, the volume that will outlast everything else he wrote and sit on kitchen shelves belonging to people with no interest in Zoroaster. The system reduces, in its own sentence, to breath and food governing thought. Strip the Persian dress off the doctrine and what is left is a nineteenth-century German hygiene manual with recipes in the back, written by a man from Posen who could have learned every word of it at home.
stops.quote: ideas and actions are controlled according to our breathing and diet.
stops.quote_source: Mazdaznan Encyclopedia of Dietetics and Home Cook Book (archive.org 'mazdaznanencyclo00hani')
suggested_refs: Mazdaznan Dietetics and Cookery Book, 1914, archive.org identifier mazdaznanencyclo00hani

stops.name: Los Angeles, the Associates of God
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the city; no address is attested for the body in 1917, and the Norton Avenue house enters the record only in 1930
stops.campa: He settles mainly in Los Angeles and founds the Reorganisierte Mazdaznan Tempel-Vereinigung der Verbuendeten Gottes, the Reorganized Mazdaznan Temple Association of the Associates of God. English summaries drop the Associates and render the last words as of God; the German name is the one the sources carry. The American headquarters is now on the Pacific, three thousand kilometres from the courtroom that convicted him. Summaries that place this founding at 1159 South Norton Avenue are running ahead of the record by thirteen years.
stops.quote: I am here upon this earth to reclaim the earth; to turn the deserts into a paradise.
suggested_refs: The Reorganisierte Mazdaznan Tempel-Vereinigung der Verbuendeten Gottes, Los Angeles, 1917

stops.name: Los Angeles, the ten indictments
stops.date_confidence: the indictments are attested to 14 June 1918; the wanted poster of 4 June is reported and unverified
stops.campa: On the fourth of June a wanted poster for him is reported circulating in Los Angeles. On the fourteenth a grand jury votes ten indictments for the sexual abuse of minors, and several of the complainants are children between eleven and fifteen years old. The poster is carried here as reported and unconfirmed; the indictments are attested. Whatever else the breathing school was, this is the charge sheet the county filed against its founder, and it is not a question of doctrine.
suggested_refs: The Los Angeles County grand jury indictments of 14 June 1918

stops.name: Chicago, the arrest and the missing verdict
stops.date_confidence: attested to early 1920; the disposition of the case is a gap, no verdict or dismissal was found
stops.campa: Early in the year he is arrested in Chicago and sent to Los Angeles to answer the indictments of 1918. What the court then did is in no source consulted: no verdict, no acquittal, no sentence, no dismissal. He is at liberty and publishing again within three years, which suggests an outcome without proving one. The disposition is a gap and it sits directly underneath the most serious charge of his life. Nothing in the movement's own literature acknowledges that the arrest happened, and the German articles do not mention it at all.
suggested_refs: Los Angeles Superior Court records for the 1918 indictments, not located

segments.name: Herrliberg and Weimar: the Movement Outruns the Man

stops.name: Leipzig, the Kingdom of Saxony names the book
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 1914 for the order, 14 May for Ammann's departure and 30 June for Frieda's
stops.campa: The Kingdom of Saxony issues an expulsion order against David Ammann and names Inner Studies, with its tantric passages, as the ground. The same book that emptied the Chicago temple two years earlier now empties the Leipzig office. Ammann leaves the city on the fourteenth of May, Frieda on the thirtieth of June. Hanish is in America and is not recorded as writing one word in his emissary's defence. A police order in Dresden and a custody hearing in Chicago reach the same verdict on the same twelve lessons, two years and one ocean apart, without either knowing of the other.
suggested_refs: The Saxon expulsion order of April 1914 against David Ammann

stops.name: Zurich, the country that takes what Germany expels
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A week after leaving Saxony, Ammann is received in Zurich. Switzerland takes what Germany expels, as it will keep doing for thirty years, and the movement acquires the country it will still be operating from when its German branch is banned outright. The Swiss chapter opens with a deportee stepping off a train, and within the year he will be looking at hillsides above the lake for a place to put a colony. Nothing places Hanish in Zurich on this day or in this year, or in this country in any year; the pin marks the movement's geography and not the founder's footsteps.
suggested_refs: Ammann's reception in Zurich, 21 May 1914

stops.name: Herrliberg, the Aryana-Heim opens
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; pin inherited byte-identical from itten.journey.json, since three conflicting Herrliberg coordinates circulate in the research
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of May the Aryana-Heim opens above the lake at Herrliberg on the Zurichsee: a Lebensschule with a farm, a diet, a press, and a colony living in it. It becomes Mazdaznan's principal European centre and outlasts the Leipzig office by decades. Ida Hofmann's hill at Ascona and this hill above Zurich are now the two Swiss addresses of German-speaking life reform. The founder of this one has never seen it and never will. Eight years from now a Bauhaus master will arrive here with his looms and take up residence in the very colony this hillside now houses.
suggested_refs: The Aryana-Heim Lebensschule at Herrliberg, opened 16 May 1915

stops.name: Vienna, the embrace of Mazdaznan
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from itten.journey.json
stops.campa: In Vienna, in the last summer of the war, the painter Johannes Itten becomes a Mazdaznan. He takes the diet, the fasting, the breathing exercises and the shaved head, and he takes them as a method of teaching and not only of living. He has never met Hanish and never will. Within three years the Chicago doctrine of breath and garlic will be running inside the most consequential art school of the century, carried there by a man who read it in translation.
suggested_refs: Itten's conversion to Mazdaznan at Vienna, 1918

stops.name: Weimar, the Mazdaznan community of the Bauhaus
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from itten.journey.json
stops.campa: At the Bauhaus, Itten's Vorkurs opens with breathing and rhythmic exercises before a pencil is lifted. Students shave their heads, wear the wide robe he designs, and eat the mashed garlic paste the school kitchen is made to produce. Georg Muche converts. Walter Gropius watches a design school acquire a religion. The teaching that Otto Haenisch of Posen assembled out of an Avesta he could not read is the morning routine at Weimar. Its founder is in Los Angeles under indictment, and no source records that he ever heard of what his book is doing in Thuringia.
suggested_refs: The Mazdaznan regime inside Itten's Vorkurs at the Weimar Bauhaus, 1919-1923

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, David Ammann dies
stops.date_confidence: attested; the place of death is contested, several accounts put it at the Herrliberg colony and the German article on Ammann puts it at Frankfurt
stops.campa: David Ammann dies at Frankfurt am Main on the twentieth of February, in unclear circumstances by the German source's own phrase, and is buried at Herrliberg cemetery on the twenty-seventh. Several accounts, including material drawn from the movement, place the death at the colony itself; the article on Ammann places it at Frankfurt. The colony is where he is buried, not where he dies, and the two dates in the record are two different towns. The European branch loses the man who actually built it, and Hanish, who has crossed the ocean once in twenty-six years, does not attend.
suggested_refs: Ammann's grave at Herrliberg cemetery, interred 27 February 1923

stops.name: Herrliberg, the Aryana community and the Ontos workshops
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from itten.journey.json
stops.campa: Gropius forces the question and Itten leaves the Bauhaus; Laszlo Moholy-Nagy takes over the Vorkurs. Itten withdraws to Herrliberg, into the Aryana settlement Ammann founded and was buried beside seven months ago, and opens the Ontos weaving workshop there. A Bauhaus master resigns his post over the doctrine, packs his household, and goes to live in the movement's Swiss colony. That much is documented. Neither man has met the other, and the doctrine that moves Itten out of Weimar reaches him through a German translation of an American book about the bowels.
suggested_refs: The Ontos weaving workshop at the Aryana settlement, Herrliberg, from 1923

stops.name: Herrliberg, the returns with no itinerary
stops.date_confidence: the pattern of regular visits from 1923 to 1932 is attested; no city, host, or date inside any year survives, and this pin is an inference
stops.campa: From this year until 1932 he returns to Europe regularly. The German source records the pattern and gives nothing else: not a city, not a host, not a date inside any of the years. The pin sits at Herrliberg because Herrliberg is by then the movement's European centre, and the placement is inference stated as inference. Nine years of crossings and not one itinerary survives, no hotel, no lecture hall, no photograph with a date on the back. By the Posen register he is sixty-six in the first of them and seventy-five in the last, and the man who invented a childhood in the Alborz leaves no record of nine real journeys.
suggested_refs: The 1923-1932 European visits recorded without itinerary in the German article

stops.name: 1159 South Norton Avenue, the draftsman's suit
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, cited to the Kansas City Star of 25 February 1930
stops.campa: Herman R. Huber, a draftsman, sues his wife for divorce and names the cult, alleging she has become fanatical, idiotical, and unreasonable by following its repugnant rituals. The papers style the defendant's teacher as Ottoman, czar of Adusht, master mind Hanisch of the Mazdazans, and give the temple address as 1159 South Norton Avenue. He is seventy-four by the Posen register and eighty-six by his own account. This is the first document that ties the movement to the Norton Avenue house.
suggested_refs: Kansas City Star, 25 February 1930, on the Huber divorce suit

stops.name: Los Angeles, Ever Creative Thought and the shelf behind it
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1931
stops.campa: Ever Creative Thought appears, one of a shelf that by now runs to dietetics, breathing, a life of Jesus rewritten as Yehoshua Nazir, and Ainyahita in Pearls, the aphorism book in which the Avestan costume fits closest to the skin. Manthra: Avesta im Lied und Gebet has been out in German since 1927. stops.name: Ascona-Moscia, the Eranos table
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Eranos pin is shared byte-identical across jung, ida_hoffmann, engelmann, arnold_rikli and antoinette_de_saint_leger, and is inherited unchanged
stops.campa: On the shore below Monte Verita, Olga Froebe-Kapteyn convenes the first Eranos conference and the hill begins its second life: scholars of religion at a long table where the vegetarians had their huts. Jung comes, and Eliade after him. The life-reform ground turns into ground for the comparative study of the sacred, which is what Hanish had been selling out of Chicago for thirty years without any of the scholarship. Ida Hofmann's huts, Engelmann's pension, and the Eranos table take one hillside in three successive tenancies, each of them teaching a version of what the last one taught.

stops.name: Leipzig, the provisional ban
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1935, within his lifetime; the literature ban follows in 1938 and the complete ban in 1941
stops.campa: The Nazi state bans Mazdaznan in Germany provisionally. Prohibition of its literature will follow in 1938 and a complete ban in 1941. The charges carried alongside the bans in the secondary literature include child abuse and antisemitic and white-supremacist material inside the teaching. They are serious, they are not adjudicated here, and the regime bringing them is not a court. Hanish is alive for the first ban, which the movement's later summaries misplace after his death. He has eleven months left, and the Swiss colony he never visited is the only part of the European structure that will still be standing in 1945.

stops.name: Los Angeles, pneumonia on a day that comes once in four years
stops.date_confidence: attested; both the English and German articles give the same date
stops.campa: He dies of pneumonia in Los Angeles on the twenty-ninth of February. No hospital, no street, no attending physician is named in any source consulted. If the Posen register is right he is seventy-nine. If his own account is right he is ninety-one. The two ages are the last thing the two biographies disagree about, and nothing in the record reconciles them. He dies twice over, at two ages, in one bed, which is the arrangement he spent forty years constructing. The date itself comes round once in four years, so most calendars will not carry his death day at all.

stops.name: Los Angeles, the grave that is not on record
stops.date_confidence: undocumented; no interment record was found and Find a Grave returned an access error in this pass
stops.campa: No cemetery record, grave marker, tomb, or interment notice for him has been found. Not in the English article, not in the German, and not at Find a Grave, whose search pages returned an access error and could not be read. A movement that ran temples on two continents and printed its founder's face in its books leaves no findable stone. The pin is the city, standing in for a fact that is missing. The gap is entered here as a gap. There is one at each end of him: no manifest for the crossing that made him American, no stone for the death that ended him.

stops.name: 1159 South Norton Avenue, the Gahanbar led by a dead man
stops.date_confidence: reported in an organizational document seen through search results only; the contradiction with the 1936 death is flagged and not resolved
stops.campa: A Mazdaznan document announces a Summer Gahanbar at the Norton Avenue temple from the twenty-seventh of June, led by Dr. O. Z. A. Hanish. He has been dead sixteen months. Either the organization went on using his name and title in the present tense to hold the congregation together, or a date is wrong somewhere in the record. The sources consulted do not decide it. The man who invented his own birth acquires, at the end, an event he presides over after his death.

stops.name: Bringhausen, the school with no Persian in its name
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1959; coordinates corrected to the village in Edertal, Landkreis Waldeck-Frankenberg
stops.campa: At Bringhausen on the Edersee in Hesse the Neuzeitliche Diaet- und Lebensschule is founded, the postwar German continuation under a name with no Persia in it. The American headquarters will move from Los Angeles to Encinitas in 1980 and go on in reduced form. What survives him is the kitchen and the breathing, unhooked from the Avesta, taught to people who have never heard the name Zar-Adusht. The temple on Norton Avenue is still listed as operating in 1960. The diet outlives the prophet, as diets do, and the Avesta goes back on the shelf it was taken from.
